comment: The evidence record for private AI company figures. One file, two readers: lib/finance/private-revenue.ts types and serves it to the financial snapshot; scripts/ingest-catalogue.mjs mines it for dated catalogue observations. Every row was mined from the AIE news feed or named-publisher reporting and then reality-checked against independent web sources before entry — publisher, date and verbatim quote required, tests enforce it, nothing carried from memory. asOf is when the figure was TRUE, not when it was republished. vendorClass separates calibration regimes: a data platform's multiple must never calibrate a frontier lab's band. Rows that failed verification did not enter: a feed item crediting Databricks with a '$4B run-rate Series K' in June 2026 contradicted both the company's own December PR ($4.8B, Series L) and CNBC's June figure ($6.9B), and was discarded as garbled.

citation.quote: Anthropic raised $30 billion in a Series G round at a $380 billion post-money valuation, led by GIC and Coatue with D. E. Shaw Ventures, Dragoneer, and Founders Fund, as run-rate revenue surged.
Anthropic raises $65B in Series H funding at $965B post-money valuation.

valuations.caveats: Led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia per the company's announcement.

citation.quote: OpenAI Valuation 2026: $852B, a 34x Revenue Multiple — after the $122B raise.

valuations.caveats: No primary company statement is in the record; three aggregators corroborate the figure, and the AIE feed independently carried a proposed 5% federal stake valued at $42.6B, which implies the same $852B. OpenAI filed confidentially on 2026-06-08 for an IPO reportedly targeting above $1 trillion.

citation.quote: Cohere raised $500 million in venture funding, achieving a $6.8 billion valuation, led by Radical Ventures and Inovia Capital.
Mistral is reportedly in talks to raise ~EUR3B at a ~EUR20B valuation, following a $830M debt facility (Mar 2026) and its ASML-led EUR1.7B Series C.

Databricks Grows >55% YoY, Surpasses $4.8B Revenue Run-Rate, and is Raising >$4B Series L at $134B Valuation — led by Insight Partners, Fidelity Management & Research Company, and J.P. Morgan Asset Management.

valuations.caveats: The PR announced the round while raising; subsequent reporting carries the Series L as closed at $134B in December 2025.

citation.quote: Databricks is in talks to raise a new funding round at a valuation between $165 billion and $175 billion, as first reported by The Information on June 9, 2026.

valuations.caveats: Reported as a $165-175B range while in talks; the top of the range is carried. Superseded within weeks by the $188B term sheet.

citation.quote: Databricks is Raising a Strategic Round of Funding at a $188 Billion Valuation — the company has signed a term sheet led by existing investor Coatue and expects the round to close later in summer 2026.

valuations.caveats: A signed term sheet, not a closed round. Everything derived from it inherits that.

citation.quote: Dario Amodei's revenue walk showed progression from $9 billion in December 2025, $14 billion in February 2026, $19 billion in March, $30 billion in April, and $44 billion in early May 2026.

revenues.caveats: One point on a company-narrated trajectory; the intermediate February, March and May points are in the same source.

citation.quote: Anthropic says it hit a $30 billion revenue run rate after 'crazy' 80x growth — run-rate revenue surpassed $30 billion in April 2026.

revenues.caveats: The AIE feed re-reported this figure on 2026-07-02 alongside the Google/Broadcom compute announcement; the figure was true in April. Dating it to the re-report would have misplaced it on the timeline.

citation.quote: Run-rate revenue crossed a reported $47 billion earlier in the month, as the company took its first formal step toward an IPO via an S-1 filing with the SEC.

revenues.caveats: Some secondary coverage recharacterised this figure as 'projected'; the company's own Series H announcement frames it as crossed. The December-to-June points ($9B, $30B, $47B) are a trajectory, not conflicting claims — earlier drafts of this record carried them as an unresolved discrepancy before the dates were verified. Claude Code alone was separately reported above a $2.5B run-rate (Anthropic, 2026-07-13).

citation.quote: OpenAI reached approximately $25 billion in annualized revenue by mid-2026, up from $21.4 billion at the end of 2025.

revenues.caveats: Third-party estimate, not a company statement.

citation.quote: OpenAI reached approximately $25 billion in annualized revenue by mid-2026 — about $17 billion from ChatGPT subscriptions, $6.5 billion from API consumption, and $1.5 billion from Sora video and licensing.

revenues.caveats: Consumer-dominant mix: roughly two-thirds is ChatGPT subscriptions, so enterprise-spend market measures cover only the API slice. The AIE feed's Fortune item framed the same period as a $25-33B range. Reported operating margin is deeply negative (~-122%), so revenue here says nothing about profit.

citation.quote: Internally, OpenAI has told investors it's targeting $30 billion in revenue for full-year 2026.

revenues.caveats: An internal target reported to investors. Projections never become the disclosed figure and never calibrate a multiple.

citation.quote: …targeting EUR1B in 2026 revenue (up from EUR200M in 2025).

revenues.caveats: Dated to the year it covers (2025 full-year revenue), reported in June 2026. Converted from EUR200M at 1.08, this product's rate.

citation.quote: …targeting EUR1B in 2026 revenue (up from EUR200M in 2025).

revenues.caveats: A target for full-year 2026, not a result. Projections never become the disclosed figure and never calibrate a multiple.

citation.quote: …with run-rate revenue reported above $400M.

revenues.caveats: TechTimes (2026-07-07) corroborates the same figure framed as ARR: 'Mistral reports over $400M in ARR'.

citation.quote: An investor memo reported by CNBC in February 2026 showed Cohere reached roughly $240 million in annual recurring revenue, beating its $200 million target, with gross margins around 70%.

revenues.caveats: Corroborated by BetaKit (2026-06-22) and a Klover.ai synthesis (2026-06-03), both citing the same CNBC memo — one underlying source, not three.

citation.quote: Databricks Grows >55% YoY, Surpasses $4.8B Revenue Run-Rate, and is Raising >$4B Series L at $134B Valuation.

revenues.caveats: Sacra independently placed end-of-2025 annualized revenue at $5.2B, consistent with this floor. AI products were separately reported at a $1.4B run-rate in Q4 2025, about 26% of total.

citation.publisher: The Information (via Tech Insider), corroborated by CNBC and Sacra
citation.quote: Databricks hit $6.9B in annualized revenue in June 2026, up from $5.4B in January 2026 and $5.2B at the end of 2025.
Databricks revenue growth tops 80% to $6.9 billion annualized.

revenues.caveats: Reported directly by CNBC and matched by Sacra's independent estimate for the same month — company statement and third-party estimate agree here.

notValuations.what: $110B in funding involving Amazon, Microsoft and Nvidia, including a $100B expansion of an AWS deal over eight years (Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-31), and the ~$300B Oracle compute agreement of September 2025
notValuations.why: Compute and infrastructure commitments, not equity rounds. They say nothing about what the company is worth or what it earns, and dividing them by a multiple would be meaningless.

notValuations.what: The sale of Colossus 1's entire ~300 MW output to Anthropic at about $1.25B per month through 2029, reported as 'potentially over $40 billion in revenue' (TechCrunch, 2026-05-20)
notValuations.why: A contracted future stream from a single customer, not reported run-rate revenue and not a valuation. It says the data centre is sold out; it does not say what xAI currently earns, so it is carried as context rather than as a figure.

notValuations.what: A merger arrangement with Germany's Aleph Alpha 'tied to a combined valuation near $20B' (TechCrunch, 2026-04-25), and a $28M U.S. DoD contract won by 'Cohere Technologies' (The Mobile Network, 2026-07-03)
notValuations.why: The $20B figure prices the combined entity, not Cohere alone. The DoD contract belongs to Cohere Technologies, a wireless OTFS company that is a different business entirely — carried here so nobody transcribes it into this record again.
